Subject: Alert: token-generation QPS spike on gen-api-us-east-1

Automated Alert: gen-api-us-east-1 observed a sustained token generation QPS increase of 3.8x above baseline for 00:09:00. Error rate increased to 1.4% (5xx + context-timeouts).

On Tue, May 4, 2027 at 09:18 Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Immediate asks:
> 1) SRE (Marissa + Mina): can you confirm whether autoscaling and burst queues reacted as expected? Any evidence of queue pile-up or KV cache saturation?

Quick triage summary (initial):
- Autoscaling: instances spun up per autoscale policy but CPU on some older instances jumped to 92% before replacement; some 30s of degraded throughput while new nodes initialized.
- Burst queue: queue backed up for ~45s peaking at ~18k inflight requests for gen-api pool; queue drain resumed once new nodes attached.
- KV cache: eviction rate increased; evidence of cache misses for long prefixes (>1k tokens) correlating with latency tail.
- Errors: 5xx spike mostly caused by overloaded runtime processes (OOM killers not observed).

Immediate mitigation we can deploy in ~20m:
A) enact a routing policy to route BrightCart traffic to a smaller model variant (latency-friendly) for requests with expected tokens >1k — this reduces per-request resource usage. No code change, just route table update.
B) hotfix the autoscaler to prefer capacity-friendly instance types first (short-term config change).

I'll attach a short runbook excerpt to INF-9123.

Marissa
Sr. Ops Lead — Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hc_packet_v1.pdf

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Alert: token-generation QPS spike on gen-api-us-east-1

Thanks team — quick notes from Eng triage:
- Hypothesis: the kernel scheduling tweak (deployed 05-03) altered our thread preemption heuristics; combined with long attention windows we see head-of-line blocking on some runtimes which amplifies tail latency under bursty token storms.
- Repro: I was able to reproduce locally with a synthetic workload (long seqs + many concurrent streams) and saw similar CPU contention.

Short-term options (tradeoffs):
1) roll back the scheduling tweak immediately (safest) — impact: ~15–30m to rollback + validation, no customer-visible config change, low risk to other regions.
2) config-based mitigation (non-rollback): temporarily change routing to prefer low-latency model variants for BrightCart and other large customers, plus enable smaller batch sizes for gen-api — impact: faster (~10m) to deploy, slightly higher per-token cost, marginally lower completion quality for extremely long prompts.
3) longer-term: rework the kernel scheduling algorithm and add contention isolation — weeks.

My recommendation: roll back the scheduling tweak for us-east immediately and simultaneously apply the routing-policy mitigation for BrightCart while we validate rollback results.

-Karthik
Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime

Copying product perspective and a draft customer note.
Product tradeoffs: we prefer not to alter model quality for BrightCart long-term; short-term routing to a lower-capacity variant is acceptable for a controlled mitigation if we clearly communicate expected behavior. Rollback of the kernel tweak is preferable if it stabilizes tail latency without customer-facing changes.

Customer note (draft):
"BrightCart — we observed a spike in token-generation requests causing elevated latency for long-sequence workloads. We are rolling back a recent runtime scheduling change and applying a short-lived routing policy to route very long requests to an alternative model variant to reduce response times. You may notice slightly different response characteristics for very long generations during the next hour; quality for shorter requests will be unaffected. We expect full restoration within 60 minutes and will follow up with a post-incident summary."

If Sales agrees, we can send this to ops@brightcart.com after the rollback job completes.

-Ben
Product Manager, Generation APIs

Hi BrightCart team,

We observed an elevated rate of token-generation requests earlier today that produced increased latency for very long sequences. Our engineering and SRE teams are taking the following actions: rollback of a runtime scheduling change deployed 05-03, and a temporary routing policy that directs very long-generation requests to an alternate model variant to reduce tail latency.

What to expect:

- We expect restoration to normal within ~60 minutes; we will send a detailed post-incident summary once we complete our analysis.
